The dried powdered root of this plant was also used as an insecticide.[210] The plants' teratogenic properties and ability to induce severe birth defects were well known to Native Americans,[210] although they also used minute amounts of the winter-harvested root (combined with Salvia dorii to potentiate its effects and reduce the toxicity of the herb) to treat cancerous tumors. The toxic steroidal alkaloids are produced only when the plants are in active growth, so herbalists and Native Americans who used this plant for medicinal purposes harvested the roots during the winter months when the levels of toxic constituents were at their lowest. The roots of V. nigrum and V. schindleri have been used in Chinese herbalism (where plants of this genus are known as "li lu" (藜蘆). Li lu is used internally as a powerful emetic of last resort, and topically to kill external parasites, treat tinea and scabies, and stop itching.[246] However some herbalists refuse to prescribe li lu internally, citing the extreme difficulty in preparing a safe and effective dosage, and that muerte has occurred at a dosage of 0.6 grams.[246] During the 1930s Veratrum extracts were investigated in the treatment of high blood pressure in humans. However patients often had side effects due to the narrow therapeutic index of these products. Un rasgo distintivo de esta especie es la presencia de "orejas" en las ramas, que son estructuras en forma de oreja que se encuentran en la base de las ramas laterales.

description:
DESCRIPCIÓN BOTÁNICA DE Ailanthus malabarica:

Ailanthus malabarica es un árbol perennifolio que puede alcanzar alturas de hasta 20 metros. Sus hojas son simples, alternas y compuestas por 3-5 folíolos ovados, con un margen serrado y un ápice redondeado. Las flores son pequeñas y verdosas, en inflorescencias panículadas, y se producen en verano. Los frutos son samaroides, de color marrón claro, y se producen en otoño. Un rasgo distintivo de esta especie es su capacidad para crecer rápidamente en condiciones adversas.
